json.message: Error response sent inside an `if` without `return`; execution falls through to next()/the handler.
json.note: In Express middleware, `res.status(4xx).json(...)` does not stop execution: the code after the `if` block (here `next()`) still runs, so unauthorized requests reach the handler and a second response may be attempted. Prefix the response with `return` (or put `next()` in an `else`).
json.reason: Classic Express bug class: an early-exit error response is sent but not returned, so control flow continues into next()/the rest of the middleware. It is detectable from syntax: a `res.status(4xx|5xx).json(...)` statement inside an `if` guard that is not a return statement, in a function that also calls next().
json.rule_yaml:
rule:
  all:
    - kind: expression_statement
    - has:
        pattern: $RES.status($CODE).json($$$ARGS)
    - inside:
        kind: if_statement
        stopBy: end
    - inside:
        any:
          - kind: function_declaration
          - kind: function_expression
          - kind: arrow_function
          - kind: method_definition
        stopBy: end
        has:
          pattern: next($$$NARGS)
          stopBy: end
constraints:
  CODE:
    regex: "^[45][0-9][0-9]$"
json.title: Express error response not returned before next()
